thread:
customer_jane: Hi — over the last hour we've had ~20 requests return 401 from our Dedicated instance. No request IDs show up in our app logs. Also seeing a few 200s that had 1.5–2s token latency spikes. Can you help?
sarah_support: Sorry you're hitting this — we can get a repro faster if you send any request IDs or a debug snapshot. Two quick asks: a) a minimal curl that reproduces (if possible) and b) time window + any customer-side request id you have.
kevin_eng: If no request id in app logs, check the SDK debug output; we surface a header named `X-RW-REQUEST-ID` (uppercase variants and `x-request-id` are accepted by gateways). Also our Console stores the server-side trace id — next steps below.
ash_mobdev: For mobile/webview: if you can reproduce, please grab a HAR or use the SDK debug logger. On Android WebView run `adb logcat | grep RWRequest` while hitting the endpoint — the SDK prints the request id as `rw_request_id=<uuid>`.
luis_se: Console path: go to Console -> Requests -> filter by time range. Click any request row, top-right shows "Request ID" and a link "Copy trace token". If you can't find it, try filtering by client IP or route name.
sarah_support: Minimal curl we ask for (replace placeholders):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-RW-REQUEST-ID: $(uuidgen || echo \"manual-123\")" \
  -d '{"input":"hello world"}' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```
Include the full verbose output (headers + body). If you get 401, copy the `X-RW-REQUEST-ID` value back into this thread.
customer_jane: We don't run uuidgen on our CI — we can pass our internal trace id in that header. Is that sufficient?
kevin_eng: Yes — any stable client-side id is fine. If you can't add a header, include the timestamp (with timezone), the approximate client IP, and the endpoint path — we can search server logs for matching entries.
nash_mobdev: If the request id isn't present, fetch a debug snapshot from Console: Console -> Support -> Create debug snapshot. Select: include SDK logs, network HAR, and enable "preserve sensitive headers" (we'll redact the token but keep request ids). Attach the snapshot file here or upload to the support portal.
sarah_support: When you send artifacts, please: 1) mark the exact time range (start/end), 2) give one example request id if you have it (client or server), 3) add a minimal curl (or HAR), and 4) confirm whether this is a Dedicated/VPC instance.
luis_se: Quick triage checklist for us once you send it: - verify auth header reached our edge - check token lookup + user mapping - inspect per-request routing (for fallback model variants) - look for 401 cause (expired key vs. upstream auth) and latency hotspots (queueing or model spin-up).
oncall_bot: incident created #INC-2026-1982 for this thread — assignment: kevin_eng.
sarah_support: If it's urgent and you can reproduce, set a repro window and we'll tail logs live. Otherwise send the snapshot and curl above and we'll take it from there :thumbsup:
customer_jane: Thanks — uploading HAR + a small log snippet and our internal trace ids now. I'll include the exact 5-minute window where this hit.
sarah_support: Got it — we'll confirm receipt and update within the hour. If we need more, we'll ask for a short screen recording showing Console -> Requests -> the missing trace (helps if the token was truncated).
